title: Higher direct images for quasi-compact quasi-separated morphisms
statement:
Let $u:U\to V$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] of schemes and let $F$ be an etale abelian
sheaf on $U$. Then for every $q\geq0$ the sheaf $R^qu_*F$ of
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is the sheafification of the presheaf on the
small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] of $V$

$$
 W\longmapsto H^q(W\times_VU,F|)
 \qquad(W\to V\text{ etale}),
$$

and on $\Dplus(U_{\Et})$ the derived direct image $Ru_*$ is computed in each
degree by the same description, applied to a K-injective resolution
[def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions].

proof.text: Apply the proved higherDirectImageSheafifiedPresheaf to f, F and q. Its presheaf, including the derived restriction maps, is exactly the first clause. The qcqs hypotheses are harmless specializations of its arbitrary-morphism statement.

For the given K-injective I put C = lowerStar(f)(I) and L = sheafToPresheaf(C). The definition of lowerStar identifies L with precomposition of the underlying presheaf complex of I along etale base change. Precomposition is exact since limits and colimits of presheaves are pointwise. Apply ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso to this precomposition functor, identifying the displayed presheaf with H^q(L), naturally in every restriction map.

Apply ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso to exact presheafToSheaf and the short complex L.sc(q). The sheafification counit sheafificationNatIso, mapped termwise, identifies sheafification(L) with C. Taking homology gives sheafification(H^q(L)) isomorphic to H^q(C).

The source-library Functor.rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso I is the K-injective computation of derived direct image: Rf_*(Q I) is isomorphic to Q(C). Invert it and transport along the supplied Q I isomorphic to K.obj. Compose with the inverse of rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility at K. Apply DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor, preceded by the inverse of homologyFunctorFactors at C. Compose with the preceding sheafification isomorphism to obtain the second clause for every integer q. No resolution is chosen, no strict lower bound on I is assumed, and no restriction-preserves-K-injectives result is needed.
